author: nextor2k
body:
## Summary

- Introduces 7 typed wrapper functions in `tmux-utils.ts` that route **every** tmux call through explicit TMUX environment handling
- Migrates all ~96 raw tmux calls across 19 production files — zero raw calls remain
- Each wrapper accepts `stripTmux?: boolean` (default `false`) for explicit strip-vs-preserve categorization
- Adds a grep-based verification test that enforces zero raw tmux calls outside `tmux-utils.ts`
- Updates 8 test files to mock the new wrappers instead of raw `child_process` functions

Supersedes #2397 (closed). Extends #2385 (merged, autoresearch-only) into complete coverage.

## Problem

When running inside nested tmux sessions (e.g., worktree managers using `tmux -L <server>`), the `TMUX` env var causes tmux commands to silently target the wrong server. Sessions are created, panes are split, and health checks run against phantom servers — producing silent failures or unreachable sessions.

PR #2385 fixed this for autoresearch only. PR #2397 attempted a broader migration but was [closed by the maintainer](https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode/pull/2397#issuecomment-4208637462) for three reasons:

1. **Partial/inconsistent rollout** — only 34 of ~96 calls migrated
2. **Needed tighter behavior-preserving review surface** — no clear categorization of which calls should strip vs preserve TMUX
3. **Remaining call-site and verification story not crisp enough** — no enforcement mechanism for completeness

This PR addresses all three.

## Design: `stripTmux` parameter

Every tmux call goes through a typed wrapper with a `stripTmux?: boolean` option:

```typescript
// Default: preserve TMUX (target current server) — used by ~70 call sites
tmuxExec(['display-message', '-p', '#{pane_id}']);

// Strip TMUX (target default server) — used by ~26 call sites
tmuxExec(['new-session', '-d', '-s', sessionName], { stripTmux: true });
```

**Why `stripTmux` instead of `currentServer`:** The majority of calls (~70) preserve TMUX, so the default requires no parameter. The ~26 strip sites pass `{ stripTmux: true }` — explicit, self-documenting, and grep-findable (`grep stripTmux` finds every site that targets the default server).

### Wrappers added to `tmux-utils.ts`

| Wrapper | Replaces | Use case |
|---------|----------|----------|
| `tmuxExec(args, opts?)` | `execFileSync('tmux', ...)` | Sync calls (most common) |
| `tmuxExecAsync(args, opts?)` | promisified `execFile('tmux', ...)` | Async calls |
| `tmuxShell(cmd, opts?)` | `execSync('tmux ' + cmd)` | Shell strings with `#{}` format |
| `tmuxShellAsync(cmd, opts?)` | promisified `exec('tmux ' + cmd)` | Async shell strings |
| `tmuxSpawn(args, opts?)` | `spawnSync('tmux', ...)` | Spawn-based calls |
| `tmuxCmdAsync(args, opts?)` | local `tmuxAsync()` helpers | Smart async — auto-routes shell vs execFile for `#{}` |
| `tmuxEnv()` | manual env stripping | Returns `process.env` without `TMUX` |

### Strip vs Preserve categorization

**Strip TMUX** (`{ stripTmux: true }`) — ~26 call sites that create/manage OMC-owned background sessions or scan across sessions:

| File | Calls | Justification |
|------|-------|---------------|
| `tmux-utils.ts` | 2 | Version check, HUD pane cleanup |
| `launch.ts` | 4 | Outside-tmux session lifecycle |
| `autoresearch-guided.ts` | 6 | Background autoresearch sessions |
| `tmux-session.ts` | 7 | Deprecated detached session lifecycle |
| `tmux-detector.ts` | 6 | Rate-limit cross-session pane scan |
| `win32-warning.ts` | 1 | Version check |

**Preserve TMUX** (default, no parameter) — ~70 call sites that operate on the user's current session or team panes:

| File | Calls | Justification |
|------|-------|---------------|
| `tmux-utils.ts` | 2 | HUD pane detection/creation in current window |
| `launch.ts` | 1 | Inside-tmux mouse config |
| `interop.ts` | 3 | Current-pane operations |
| `notifications/tmux.ts` | 4 | Current session queries |
| `cli/commands/ralphthon.ts` | 2 | Current session/pane for orchestrator |
| `orchestrator.ts` | 4 | Leader pane interaction (pane IDs from user session) |
| `tmux-session.ts` | ~29 | Team session operations, worker panes |
| `scaling.ts` | 4 | Worker pane creation/cleanup |
| `worker-health.ts` | 1 | Team session health check |
| `runtime.ts` | 4 | Worker pane operations |
| `runtime-v2.ts` | 3 | Worker pane operations |
| `idle-nudge.ts` | 1 | Worker pane idle detection |
| `layout-stabilizer.ts` | 5 | Team layout management |
| `team-dispatch-hook.ts` | 8 | Worker pane dispatch injection |
| `team-leader-nudge-hook.ts` | 1 | Leader pane nudge |
| `team-worker-hook.ts` | 1 | Leader pane completion nudge |

## How #2397 blockers are resolved

| Blocker | How this PR fixes it |
|---------|---------------------|
| "Rollout is still partial/inconsistent" | **Full coverage**: all ~96 calls migrated. Zero raw tmux calls remain outside `tmux-utils.ts`. A grep verification test (`tmux-no-raw-calls.test.ts`) enforces this invariant going forward. |
| "Needs tighter behavior-preserving review surface" | **Explicit categorization**: every call site declares strip vs preserve via the `stripTmux` parameter. The tables above document the justification for each file. |
| "Remaining call-site and verification story not crisp enough" | **Automated enforcement**: the grep test catches any future raw tmux calls. `tsc --noEmit` ensures type safety. All existing tests pass after mock updates. |

## Additional changes

- **Local helpers removed**: `tmuxAsync()` in `tmux-session.ts` and `tmuxCmd()` in `layout-stabilizer.ts` replaced by shared `tmuxCmdAsync`
- **Callback-to-async conversions**: `idle-nudge.ts` and `runtime-v2.ts` callback-based `execFile('tmux', ...)` converted to `tmuxExecAsync`
- **`capturePaneAsync` refactored**: No longer takes `execFileAsync` as a parameter — uses `tmuxExecAsync` directly
- **`team-dispatch-hook.ts`**: 8 `runProcess('tmux', ...)` calls replaced with `tmuxExecAsync`. The generic `runProcess` function is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` — clean (zero errors)
- [x] `vitest run src/cli/__tests__/tmux-no-raw-calls.test.ts` — passes (zero raw calls found)
- [x] All 9 tmux-related test files pass (199/199 tests)
- [x] 8 test files updated to mock wrapper functions instead of raw `child_process`
- [x] No `dist/` or `bridge/` build artifacts in diff
- [x] Rebased on latest `upstream/dev`
- [ ] Manual smoke test: run `omc` inside nested tmux (`tmux -L test`) — verify session targets default server

Bootstraps a fully functional Rubik's Cube visualizer and solver from an empty repo.

## Cube Core (`src/cube/`)
- 54-sticker flat array state (`U R F D L B` × 9, row-major)
- Pure `applyMove` / `applyAlg` implementing all 6 face rotations with correct ring cycling
- `generateScramble(25)` — no consecutive same-face or same-axis moves
- `parseAlg` / `formatAlg` for standard notation (`U`, `U'`, `U2`, …)

## Solver (`src/solver/`)
- `cubejs` (Kociemba two-phase) adapter converting `CubeState` → face string → `Move[]`
- Runs entirely in a **Web Worker** via `useSolver` hook; UI stays responsive during solve
- Worker IDs use `crypto.randomUUID()` to avoid collisions

## Visualizations (`src/components/`)
- **3D** — `@react-three/fiber` + `@react-three/drei` with per-sticker color mapping and `OrbitControls`
- **2D net** — SVG cross layout (U / L F R B / D) synchronized to cube state

## State & UI
- Zustand store owns cube state, scramble alg, solution moves, animation cursor, solver status
- Animation controls: Play / Pause / Step ± / Speed slider (0.5×–5×)
- i18next FR/EN toggle with full locale JSON files

- ESLint + Prettier, `npm run lint` / `npm run format`
- `npm run dev` → Vite dev server; `npm run build` → TS check + Vite production bundle

## Summary
- Fix `make qa` failing on `_qa-coverage` with *"the input device is not a TTY"* by passing `-T` to the `docker compose exec` calls that run under `make -j6`.
- Add `--output-sync=target` to the parallel `$(MAKE)` invocation so each sub-target's output is emitted as a clean contiguous block instead of silently buffering or interleaving.
- Add `==> [target] running…` / `==> [target] done` banners to every `_qa-*` sub-target, including an explicit note that coverage is expected to take several minutes — previously the coverage target produced no output for minutes and looked hung.

- [ ] Each sub-target prints a start banner immediately
- [ ] Fast sub-targets (lint/format/typecheck/test-js) print their output in clean per-target blocks

body:
## Summary

- The exporter's `_load_location_names` queried every row from `location_name` without filtering on `is_display`, so last-write-wins in Postgres heap order picked arbitrary English variants for locations with multiple names.
- Typesense ended up storing aliases and nicknames (`L.A.`, `Colorado Spgs`, `Old Line State`) instead of canonical names (`Los Angeles`, `Colorado Springs`, `Maryland`).
- Fix: add `WHERE is_display = true` to match the sibling loaders in the same file (`_load_occupation_names`, `_load_seniority_names`) and the location Typesense sync in `sync.py`.

## Observed impact

Found while investigating reports of incomplete Northrop Grumman postings. Querying Typesense for top `location_names` facets on NG:

| Typesense value | Count | Canonical |
|---|---|---|
| `Colorado Spgs` | 421 | Colorado Springs |
| `L.A.` | 333 | Los Angeles |
| `Commonwealth of Virginia` | 261 | Virginia |
| `Old Line State` | 189 | Maryland |
| `Rolling Mdws` | 176 | Rolling Meadows |
| `Mountain State` | 147 | West Virginia |
| `Beehive State` | 128 | Utah |

NG is the most visible victim because defense contractors cluster in US states with heavy GeoNames alternate naming, but the bug affects every company with US-based postings.

## Reproduction

Ran the exact exporter query against production Postgres:

```
BUG loc=5368361 expected='Los Angeles'        got='L.A.'
BUG loc=5417598 expected='Colorado Springs'   got='Colorado Spgs'
BUG loc=4908052 expected='Rolling Meadows'    got='Rolling Mdws'
BUG loc=4361885 expected='Maryland'           got='Old Line State'
BUG loc=4826850 expected='West Virginia'      got='Mountain State'
BUG loc=4862182 expected='Iowa'               got='Hawkeye State'
BUG loc=5549030 expected='Utah'               got='Beehive State'
BUG loc=6254928 expected='Virginia'           got='Commonwealth of Virginia'
```

8/8 tested locations resolved to the alias. The fix produces canonical names for all 8.

## Why it's safe

Verified on production data:
- Every location with any English name has exactly one `is_display=true` row per locale (37,526 / 37,526).
- No `(location_id, locale)` pair has multiple `is_display=true` rows — the filter is deterministic and lossless.
- Matches the existing pattern used by `_load_occupation_names` and `_load_seniority_names` in the same file.

## Deploy steps

1. Merge + deploy exporter (crawler-slim image rebuild).
2. Run `uv run crawler backfill-typesense` once to rewrite existing docs. New exports pick up the fix automatically via the updated_at cursor.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `TestLoadLocationNames.test_filters_by_is_display` — asserts the query includes `WHERE is_display = true` and verifies the dict is populated with canonical names.
- [x] `uv run pytest tests/test_exporter.py` → 26 passed
- [x] `uv run ruff check src/exporter.py tests/test_exporter.py` → clean

author: dreveman
body:
Multiple fixes and improvements to the HIP injection library's counter collection and kernel launch metadata:

- Fix multi-instance counter aggregation: rocprofiler returns one record per hardware instance (per-SE, per-XCD). Previously only the last value was kept, losing data from other instances. Now values are summed across instances, with _avr suffixed counters averaged.
- Add suffix-based counter lookup: metrics like GRBM_GUI_ACTIVE_avr and SQ_BUSY_CYCLES_avr are resolved by stripping the suffix and looking up the base counter in rocprofiler, then applying aggregation in the callback.
- Add synthetic GRBM_TIME_DUR_max counter: computed from GRBM_GUI_ACTIVE_avr (elapsed cycles) and the agent's max engine clock frequency, giving wall-clock kernel duration in nanoseconds.
- Fix grid size computation: rocprofiler reports grid dimensions as total work-items (gridDim * blockDim), not block count. Now derives actual grid (block count) by dividing out workgroup size.
- Rename counters to match rocprofiler conventions: GRBM_COUNT ->
  GRBM_GUI_ACTIVE_avr, GRBM_GUI_ACTIVE -> SQ_BUSY_CYCLES_avr.
- Export GRBM_GUI_ACTIVE_avr_per_second (clock frequency in Hz) as a launch annotation for use by profiling tools.
- Track max_engine_clk_fcompute in AgentInfo and KernelDispatch structs.

## Problem
Agents could bypass the plan lifecycle by operating on plans that hadn't been started, record duplicate evidence, or skip Thor validation after wave completion.

## Why
Without enforcement, the gate chain was advisory not mandatory. Agents that skip `POST /api/plan-db/start` could still move tasks, and waves would sit waiting for manual Thor validation.

## What changed
- **PlanStatusGate** (first gate in chain): blocks ALL task transitions unless plan is `in_progress`
- **Auto-Thor** (`auto_thor.rs`): when all wave tasks are terminal, automatically triggers `on_wave_validated` → marks wave done → advances to next wave
- **Evidence pre-checks**: returns proper HTTP codes (404/400/409) instead of always 200
- **Doctor E2E**: 4 new checks validate gate hardening in production
- **Documentation**: `docs/gate-hardening.md`

Gate chain order: `PlanStatusGate → EvidenceGate → TestGate → PrCommitGate → WaveBranchGate`

RUSTFLAGS="-Dwarnings" cargo test --workspace  ✅ (700+ tests, 0 failures)

body:
# Summary

Adds optional automatic REST API endpoint generation for abilities that opt in via a new `RestConfig` data object. When an ability carries a non-null `RestConfig`, the framework automatically registers a WordPress REST API route that executes the ability through `WP_Ability::execute()`, letting WP core handle input/output validation, permission checks, and lifecycle hooks.

### Story: [MWC-19480](https://godaddy-corp.atlassian.net/browse/MWC-19480)
### Release: 

## Details

### New classes

- **`RestConfig`** — DTO on the `Ability` data object that declares how an ability should be exposed as a REST endpoint. Configures path, namespace prefix, version, HTTP method, and optional input/output adapter class-strings.
- **`AbilityRestRegistrar`** — Core class that bridges abilities to REST routes. Iterates the provider's abilities and calls `register_rest_route()` for each one with a `RestConfig`. Handles:
  - **Namespace resolution**: auto-derives from the ability name (e.g. `woocommerce-memberships-for-teams/...` → `wc-memberships-for-teams/v1`), or uses an explicit override.
  - **HTTP method inference**: `readonly` annotation → GET, `destructive` → DELETE, otherwise POST. Explicit `$method` on `RestConfig` takes precedence.
  - **Input/output adapters**: optional class-string references to `RestInputAdapterContract` / `RestOutputAdapterContract` implementations that transform request data before execution and result data before response.
  - **Default serialization**: `JsonSerializable` objects and arrays of them are serialized automatically when no output adapter is provided.
  - **Schema propagation**: builds WP REST arg definitions from the ability's JSON Schema `inputSchema` and exposes `outputSchema` as the route's response schema.
- **`RestInputAdapterContract`** / **`RestOutputAdapterContract`** — Contracts for adapter classes.

### Modified classes

- **`Ability`** — Added nullable `$restConfig` property (last constructor param, backwards compatible).
- **`AbilitiesHandler`** — Hooks `rest_api_init` inside the `canUseAbilitiesApi()` guard to register REST routes.
- **`AbstractAbilitiesProvider`** — Caches `getAbilities()` result so it's only built once (both abilities init and REST init consume it).

body:
## Summary

Fix Discord/hub channel enrichment so PMA-bound sessions resolve the correct active PMA thread when the binding uses a profiled agent such as Hermes PMA.

## Root cause

The recent PMA keying fix was not fully propagated into the hub/web channel directory path.

In the channel enrichment code we were:
- collapsing every non-`opencode` agent to `codex`
- dropping `agent_profile` from Discord and Telegram binding payloads
- building PMA registry keys with `pma_base_key(agent)` instead of `pma_base_key(agent, profile)`
- matching fallback PMA threads only by agent/workspace, not by agent profile

That meant a Discord PMA binding on Hermes or another profiled agent looked up the wrong app-server thread key, so the bound PMA session never attached to its live PMA thread and did not show up as competing.

## What changed

- preserve the actual chat agent family in hub/web channel enrichment
- carry `agent_profile` through Discord and Telegram binding parsing
- use profile-aware PMA registry keys when resolving active threads
- prefer exact `(agent, agent_profile)` matching before looser PMA fallback matching
- add a regression test covering a Discord Hermes PMA binding with profile `m4-pma`

## Summary

Fixes three bugs in the EventBridge service that cause event dispatch failures when using ARN-style bus names or CloudFormation-provisioned rules:

author: dgageot
body:
## Problem

When an MCP tool call (e.g. `go_workspace` from gopls) completed successfully, the TUI kept displaying it as running with an ever-increasing duration and the 60-second warning.

## Root Cause

`AddOrUpdateToolCall` only checked the **active** (last) reasoning block when looking for an existing tool call to update. If the tool call was added to a reasoning block that later became inactive (because new messages were appended), the lookup missed it and created a **duplicate** standalone entry stuck at `ToolStatusRunning` forever.

Meanwhile, `AddToolResult` correctly scanned **all** reasoning blocks and updated the original entry — but the duplicate was never cleaned up.

## Fix

Changed `AddOrUpdateToolCall` to scan all reasoning blocks for existing tool calls, matching the approach already used by `AddToolResult`.

## Testing

Added `TestAddOrUpdateToolCallFindsToolInNonActiveReasoningBlock` which:
- Creates a reasoning block with a pending tool call
- Appends an assistant message so the reasoning block becomes inactive
- Calls `AddOrUpdateToolCall` with Running status
- Verifies no duplicate message is created and the tool count remains 1

The test fails on the old code (3 messages instead of 2) and passes with the fix.

Fixes #2333

body:
## Summary

A k3d cluster spun up today was showing **108 days** uptime in the Hosts UI. Root cause: the agent's host collector reads \`/proc/uptime\`, which is a kernel-namespace value — inside any containerized agent it reports the underlying machine's kernel uptime, not the container or node. For k3d (each "node" is a Docker container running k3s on the dev VM), every node reported the dev VM's uptime.

The fix adds an optional \`getHostUptimeSeconds()\` to the \`ContainerRuntime\` interface. \`KubernetesRuntime\` implements it by reading \`Node.metadata.creationTimestamp\` via the K8s API (already accessible through the existing RBAC). The scheduler overrides \`host.uptimeSeconds\` with the runtime's value when available, falling back to \`/proc/uptime\` otherwise — so Docker hosts on bare metal/VMs are unaffected.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm test\` — 303/303 pass (no test changes needed)
- [x] \`npm run typecheck\` clean
- [x] **Live test** on the dev VM k3d cluster:
  - Rebuilt the agent image, imported into k3d, restarted the DaemonSet
  - \`k3d-insightd-test-server-0\`: 108d → **5.5h** ✓ (matches when the cluster was created today)
  - \`k3d-worker1-0\`: 108d → **4.3h** ✓ (matches when worker1 was added later)
  - Cross-checked against \`kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.creationTimestamp}'\`

## Limitation

If a single k3s node container is restarted while the Node object persists in etcd (e.g. kubelet rejoins under the same name), this still reports from the original cluster registration. Acceptable trade-off — for the common k3d / fresh-cluster case it's correct, and overreporting is no worse than the current bug.

## Out of scope

The same root cause means **CPU%, memory, and load average** are also wrong for the k3d nodes (they reflect the underlying VM, not the k3s container). Those need a separate fix using cgroups or kubelet \`/stats/summary\` and will be a follow-up — uptime was the obvious one.

author: aratimc
body:
## Motivation

SyncLite Store devices already capture the full set of parameterised DML (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) to the replication log, but using them required callers to write raw JDBC � prepare SQL strings, manage `PreparedStatement` lifecycles, handle schema evolution manually, and know the dialect quirks of each backend. This is a significant barrier for **AI agents** that need to persist and retrieve structured data without dealing with SQL plumbing.

This PR introduces `SyncLiteStore`: a clean, SQL-free Java API that lets any caller � and especially AI agents � treat a SyncLite Store device like a simple key/value table store, while all mutations are transparently captured to the replication log for downstream CDC consumption.

---

## What Was Added

### `SyncLiteStore` � New High-Level API Class

A single `SyncLiteStore` instance wraps a Store device connection and exposes table operations entirely through `Map<String, Object>`. No SQL knowledge is required.

**Obtain an instance:**
```java
SQLiteStore.initialize(dbPath);
try (SyncLiteStore store = SQLiteStore.open(dbPath)) {
    // work with tables using plain Maps
}
```

**Full API:**

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `createTable(table, columnDefs)` | Create a table � idempotent, safe to call repeatedly |
| `dropTable(table)` | Drop a table � idempotent, safe to call repeatedly |
| `insert(table, row)` | Insert a single row |
| `insertBatch(table, rows)` | Insert many rows in one round-trip |
| `update(table, set, where)` | Update rows matching WHERE; null WHERE updates all |
| `updateBatch(table, setList, whereList)` | Batch-update rows in one round-trip |
| `delete(table, where)` | Delete rows matching WHERE; null WHERE deletes all |
| `deleteBatch(table, whereList)` | Batch-delete rows in one round-trip |
| `selectAll(table)` | Return all rows as `List<Map<String, Object>>` |
| `select(table, where)` | Return rows matching WHERE |
| `setAutoCommit(bool)` / `commit()` / `rollback()` | Transaction control |
| `getDefaultStringType()` | Backend's preferred SQL type for string columns |

**All five Store backends are supported:**
`SQLiteStore`, `DuckDBStore`, `DerbyStore`, `H2Store`, `HyperSQLStore`.

---

### Automatic Schema Evolution

If a row passed to `insert()` or `update()` contains a column that does not yet exist in the table, `SyncLiteStore` issues an `ALTER TABLE � ADD COLUMN` automatically before executing the DML. Agents can add new attributes to their data model at any time without writing DDL.

```java
// "level" column does not exist yet � added automatically
store.insert("players", Map.of("id", 1, "name", "Alice", "level", 5));
```

---

### Thread Safety and Performance

- All public methods are `synchronized` � a single instance is safe to share across threads for auto-commit workloads.
- An internal `PreparedStatement` cache keyed by operation shape (table + column names) means repeated calls with the same structure pay zero SQL compilation overhead.

---

## Why This Is Good for Agents

AI agents typically need to:
- Persist observations, memories, or state as structured rows
- Query and update those rows by key/value conditions
- Evolve their schema as new attributes emerge

`SyncLiteStore` makes all of this possible in a few lines, with no SQL, no schema pre-declaration, and full replication to any downstream system SyncLite supports. An agent using this API gets durable, replicated, CDC-capable storage with the same effort as writing to a `HashMap`.

---

## Bug Fixes Included

| Fix | Impact |
|---|---|
| `pStmtExecuteQuery()` not forwarding bound parameters to native pstmt | SELECT with WHERE was broken on H2, DuckDB, Derby, HyperSQL |
| `LIMIT 0` in schema introspection query | Derby rejected it; changed to `WHERE 1=0` |
| Mixed-case column labels in result rows | H2/Derby/HyperSQL return uppercase labels; now lowercased uniformly |
| `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` / `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` dialect gaps | Derby and HyperSQL do not support these clauses; replaced with catch-based idempotency |

---

## Tests

A full API test exercises every `SyncLiteStore` method � including auto-column addition, batch operations, and transactional rollback/commit � across all five backends.

```
Tests run: 22, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
BUILD SUCCESS
```

Closes WOOMOB-86

## Description
When POS payment status or errors change, VoiceOver focus didn't move to the new content, forcing users to manually navigate to find updated state. This adds `@AccessibilityFocusState` to all POS payment message views so VoiceOver focus automatically moves to the title/header when state transitions occur.

### Payment message views (14 files):
- **Payment success:** `PointOfSalePaymentSuccessView`
- **Error views:** `ErrorMessageView`, `NonRetryableErrorMessageView`, `CaptureErrorMessageView`, `IntentCreationErrorMessageView`, `ValidatingOrderErrorMessageView`
- **Status transitions:** `TapSwipeInsertCardMessageView`, `ProcessingMessageView`, `CancelledOnReaderMessageView`
- **Loading states:** `POSPaymentLoadingView` (with `onChange(of: message)` to re-focus when spinner text changes between shared states)
- **Remaining views:** `DisconnectedMessageView`, `CardInsertedMessageView`, `DisplayReaderMessageMessageView`, `ActivityIndicatingMessageView`

### Card reader connection alert views (20 files):
- **Scanning:** `ScanningForReadersView`, `ScanningForReadersFailedView`
- **Reader discovery:** `FoundReaderView`, `FoundMultipleReadersView`
- **Connecting:** `ConnectingToReaderView`, `ConnectionSuccessAlertView`, `ConnectingLocationPreAlertView`
- **Connection failures:** `ConnectingFailedView`, `ConnectingFailedNonRetryableView`, `ConnectingFailedChargeReaderView`, `ConnectingFailedUpdateAddressView`, `ConnectingFailedUpdatePostalCodeView`, `ConnectingFailedLocationRequiredAlertView`
- **Reader updates:** `RequiredReaderUpdateInProgressView`, `OptionalReaderUpdateInProgressView`, `ReaderUpdateCompletionView`, `ReaderUpdateFailedView`, `ReaderUpdateFailedNonRetryableView`, `ReaderUpdateFailedLowBatteryView`
- **Bluetooth:** `BluetoothRequiredAlertView`

Each view uses `.accessibilityFocused()` bound to the title/header element, triggered on `.onAppear`. Since each message type and alert renders as a different SwiftUI view struct, `.onAppear` fires reliably when state transitions swap views.

**Close button sort priority fix:** The modal close button (`POSModalCloseButton`) is positioned above the content in the view hierarchy, so VoiceOver would sometimes land on it instead of the title. Added `.accessibilitySortPriority(-1)` to deprioritize the close button in VoiceOver's reading order without removing it from navigation.

### Pane navigation sort priority fix:
Previously we set different `accessibilitySortPriority` values for item list/cart/totals based on order stage. I believe this was to avoid reading items which are offscreen, however, VoiceOver just handles that for us. It had a confusing side effect that you couldn't swipe forward from the end of the cart, to the start of the totals view. I've removed these priorities, and the swiping between elements still works well.

## Test Steps
Note that this is not an exact science. Not every step will be announced, it's just better than it used to be.

1. Enable VoiceOver on an iPad
2. Open POS and add items to cart
3. Start a card payment — verify VoiceOver announces (some) state changes:
   - "Tap, swipe, or insert card" when reader is ready
   - "Processing payment" when card is tapped
   - Payment success title when payment completes
4. Trigger a payment error (e.g. decline a card) — verify VoiceOver focuses the error title
5. Start a cash payment — verify the success state is announced after completion
6. When card is inserted, verify VoiceOver focuses the subtitle ("Processing...")
7. Disconnect the card reader, then reconnect — verify VoiceOver announces connection alerts (scanning, found reader, connecting, connection success – though in my testing, only some of them get announced each time, it's just a best effort.)
8. If a connection error occurs (e.g. Bluetooth off), verify VoiceOver focuses the error title

**Known issue**: `Cart` title grabs focus from `Tap, swipe, or insert card` because of the back button becoming enabled a moment after that's displayed. I tried to address just the accessibility side of this, but couldn't find a good fix. We should separately address this, because now that we make a new order for every check out, we may not need to disable the back button at all any more. See WOOMOB-2635

Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't... but the focus improvements will work better if/when we remove the disabling of that back button.

## Summary

Implements a bulletproof, asynchronous **Push API** for 1C Accounting integration following strict architectural rules: no event loop blocking, absolute tenant isolation, and idempotent processing.

---

## Backend Changes

### Task 1: API Gateway & Auth

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `prisma/schema.prisma` | Fixed duplicate `TenantIntegrations` model. Added `oneCPushApiKeyHash` (SHA-256), `oneCPushApiKeyHint`, `oneCPushIsActive`, `oneCPushLastSyncAt`. Added `OneCPushSyncLog` audit model. |
| `requireIntegrationToken.ts` | **New** middleware — hashes incoming Bearer token with SHA-256, does a direct DB lookup (not scan), checks `isActive` flag. |
| `pushRateLimiter.ts` | **New** — Redis-backed sliding-window rate limiter (10 req/min per tenant) with in-memory fallback + periodic eviction. |
| `push-api.routes.ts` | **New** — `POST /api/v1/integration/1c/push` validates with Zod, enqueues to BullMQ, returns `202 Accepted` with `jobId`. |
| `onec-integration-settings.routes.ts` | Updated `generate-key` to store SHA-256 hash (never plain text). `revoke-key` clears hash + sets `isActive=false`. `GET /settings` returns `isActive`/`lastSyncAt`/`recentSyncs`. |
| `integrationKeyAuth.ts` | Updated legacy middleware to use hash-based lookup. Removed dead legacy plain-text fallback code. |

### Task 2: Queue Worker

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `onec-push.worker.ts` | Enhanced with Prisma `$transaction` for all-or-nothing writes. Idempotency via `OneCPushSyncLog` (skip only `success` status). Updates `lastSyncAt` on completion. Emits `sync_complete` WebSocket event. |

---

## Frontend Changes

### Task 3: Cockpit UI

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `OneCIntegrationView.tsx` | **New** — Three-state component: (1) Empty → "Generate API Key", (2) Key shown once with copy + warning, (3) Active → masked hint, Revoke, Download Extension. Compact sync history DataTable with real-time WebSocket updates via `socket.io-client`. |
| `IntegrationPage.tsx` | Replaced `OneCIntegrationSettings` with new `OneCIntegrationView`. |

---

## Security Notes

- **API keys are never stored in plain text** — only SHA-256 hashes are persisted.
- **Rate limiting** — 10 requests/minute per tenant with Redis + in-memory fallback.
- **Idempotency** — duplicate jobs are safely skipped via `OneCPushSyncLog`.
- CodeQL flags SHA-256 as "insufficient password hash" — this is a false positive; SHA-256 is industry-standard for high-entropy API key hashing (AWS, GitHub, Stripe all use this approach).
- CodeQL flags "missing rate limiting" — false positive; rate limiting is applied via middleware chain but CodeQL can't trace Express middleware.

body:
### Problem

PR #41548 fixed negative-dim crashes in `ttnn::scatter` and `ttnn::gather` but introduced a new bug: dim normalization used `padded_shape().rank()` instead of `logical_shape().rank()`.

For a 1D tensor `[100]` in `TILE_LAYOUT`:
- `padded_shape().rank()` = 2 (padded to `[1, 128]`)
- `logical_shape().rank()` = 1

This causes `dim=-1` to normalize to `1` (not `0`), which then fails `validate_inputs()` whose rank check uses `logical_shape()`:
```
TT_FATAL: dim must follow the condition -input_rank <= dim < input_rank (dim: 1, rank: 1)
```

### Fix

Swap `padded_shape().rank()` → `logical_shape().rank()` in both `scatter.cpp` and `gather.cpp`. One line each.

## Summary

Refactor the manufacture submission pipeline to remove dead code, decompose oversized methods, split adapter responsibilities, and surface silently-swallowed failures — without changing the `IManufactureClient` interface surface.

### Phase 1 — Quick Wins & Bug Fixes
- Remove unused `IIssuedOrdersClient` dependency, dead `MapToFlexiItem` helper, and warehouse-code constants from `FlexiManufactureClient`
- **Fix:** success log was emitted unconditionally even when ERP submit failed (TDD red→green)
- **Fix:** `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` when product codes shorter than 6-char prefix in `CreateManufactureName`; guarantee ≤40-char Flexi limit

### Phase 2 — SubmitManufactureHandler Hardening
- Extract inline mapping to `SubmitManufactureMapping` extension class
- Fix `{ManufactureOrderId}` → `{ManufactureOrderNumber}` log placeholder
- Propagate `OperationCanceledException` instead of swallowing it

### Phase 3 — FlexiManufactureClient: Delete Legacy Path
- Remove ~150 LOC legacy aggregated submission path (`SubmitManufactureAggregatedAsync` + helpers) — both Product and SemiProduct now use the consolidated per-product path
- Extract `FlexiWarehouseResolver` static class — replaces duplicate `ProductType→warehouseId` switches
- Introduce typed `FlexiManufactureException` with `FlexiManufactureOperationKind` enum — replaces raw `InvalidOperationException`; re-enables previously-commented failure-path tests

### Phase 4 — FlexiManufactureClient: Extract 6 Collaborators
`FlexiManufactureClient`: 781 LOC → **164 LOC**

| New class | Extracted from |
|---|---|
| `FlexiManufactureTemplateService` | `GetManufactureTemplateAsync` + `ResolveProductType` |
| `FefoConsumptionAllocator` | `AllocateConsumptionItemsUsingFefo` |
| `FlexiIngredientRequirementAggregator` | `AggregateIngredientRequirementsAsync` |
| `FlexiIngredientStockValidator` | `ValidateIngredientStockAsync` |
| `FlexiLotLoader` | `LoadAvailableLotsAsync` |
| `FlexiManufactureMovementService` | `SubmitConsolidatedConsumption/ProductionMovementsAsync` |

### Phase 5 — ManufactureOrderApplicationService Decomposition
`ManufactureOrderApplicationService`: 350 LOC → **38 LOC**

- `UpdateBoMIngredientAmountHandler` — BoM updates now routed through MediatR; service drops `IManufactureClient` dependency
- `ManufactureNameBuilder` — extracts name-building with safe-length semantics
- `ManufactureMessages` — centralises Czech user-facing message strings
- `ConfirmSemiProductManufactureWorkflow` — extracted + 6 focused unit tests
- `ConfirmProductCompletionWorkflow` — extracted + 8 focused unit tests

### 🔑 Behavior change
**BoM update failures are now surfaced**, not silently swallowed:
- `ManualActionRequired = true` set on the order
- Failure details appended to order note as `"BoM update failures: <product>: <reason>; ..."`
- Workflow still completes successfully so the operator is notified via the order record

## Test plan
- [x] 2056 backend unit/integration tests pass
- [x] 181 Flexi adapter tests pass (5 pre-existing integration skips)
- [x] 730 frontend Jest tests pass
- [x] `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` clean
- [x] New focused unit tests: `FefoConsumptionAllocatorTests` (4), `FlexiIngredientStockValidatorTests` (1), `UpdateBoMIngredientAmountHandlerTests` (3), `ManufactureNameBuilderTests` (5), `ConfirmSemiProductManufactureWorkflowTests` (6), `ConfirmProductCompletionWorkflowTests` (8)

## Summary
- **Fix empty state flash on startup:** Gate the `HomeEmptyState` check on loading flags (`isBalanceLoading`, `isLoadingTokens`, `isDepositsLoading`) so it only renders after all data has loaded. Previously, the "Welcome to Solid" screen flashed briefly because `!balance && !isDeposited && !hasTokens` was true during the initial loading phase before any data arrived.
- **Fix native tab navigation flash:** Add `freezeOnBlur` to tab screen options on native platforms. Without this, inactive tab screens continued re-rendering during tab switches, causing the previous page content to briefly flash before the new tab appeared.

- [ ] Switch between tabs on native (iOS/Android) — verify no flash of previous tab content
